newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel moves ahead on Jewish housing in Arab area.
newsitem.headline: Israel moves ahead on Jewish housing in Arab area.

text.p: An Israeli planning commission approved on Tuesday the building of 132 housing units for Jews in the heart of an Arab East Jerusalem neighbourhood, an interior ministry spokeswoman said.
"Yes, that's correct," the spokeswoman said when asked to confirm a radio report. The plan will not be final until it is signed by Interior Minister Eliahu Suissa.

Palestinians and officials in Israel's former government have warned that the plan to build Jewish housing in the Ras al-Amud neighbourhood of Arab East Jerusalem could provoke a violent outburst if implemented.
Israel's opening of an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem in September touched off clashes that killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

The status of East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war along with the rest of the West Bank, is up for negotiations in final status peace talks which have yet to resume under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who took office in June.
There are now some 160,000 Jews living in East Jerusalem -- where Palestinians hope to found the capital of a future state -- amidst 155,000 Palestinians.
